messages:
alex (EngRuntime): Heads-up — FinEdge pushed back on our proposed SLO. They want p95=120ms, p99=300ms for chat endpoint under their steady QPS. We can't hit both without changes.
priya (Product): Do we have a concrete perf breakdown to show them? they want something to sign for Dedicated.
jamie (Sales): FinEdge is on a 1yr commit if we can get P99 under 300. They know p95 will be tighter.
li (PerfEng): Quick summary from today's profiling run (dev cluster, 2xA10):
```
model: rbase-chat-13B
kernel A (fused-attn): avg_token=6.2ms, p95_token=9.4ms, p99_token=28.7ms
microbatch=4 -> end-to-end p95=140ms, p99=420ms @ qps=180
microbatch=1 -> end-to-end p95=160ms, p99=260ms @ qps=60
KV cache hit ~82% reduces avg ~25ms but p99 still spikes due to tail kernels + scheduling jitter
```
li (PerfEng): TL;DR: smaller microbatch helps p99 but kills throughput; larger microbatch improves throughput and p95 but p99 spikes from stragglers. KV warmup helps p95 a lot.
carla (SRE): We also saw a few 10-30s GC pauses on the host agent causing tail amplification during the run. Not purely model kernel.
jamie (Sales): So we can promise p95=~140 easily with microbatch=4, but p99 will be >300 unless we do something special. Is a hybrid SLO possible?
priya (Product): Proposal: give FinEdge a tiered SLO: p95 140ms guaranteed, p99 best-effort with a SLA clause that allows fallback to smaller model variant or cold-start window. Thoughts?
alex (EngRuntime): Engineering options to hit p99=300: 1) per-customer microbatch cap (force microbatch=1 for their traffic) + autoscale more GPUs; 2) prioritize their requests on scheduling path (queue prioritization + preemption); 3) material KV warmup (pre-warm prefix cache on deploy); 4) fall back to a quantized low-latency model for tail tokens. All have tradeoffs on cost/throughput.
li (PerfEng): Data point: dedicating 2 extra GPUs + microbatch=1 in test gave p99 ~240ms but reduced overall throughput by ~55%.
carla (SRE): Ops note: prioritization + preemption requires scheduler changes and will increase jitter for other tenants. We'll need explicit customer isolation for Dedicated.
jamie (Sales): FinEdge is willing to pay for isolation if it gets the SLA. Need a clear cost delta. Can you estimate engineering + infra delta?
alex (EngRuntime): Rough cost sketch: isolation + 2x GPUs -> +42% infra cost. Engineering work ~2 sprint tickets (scheduler + per-customer config) to get safe rollout.
priya (Product): Let's offer two options to FinEdge: (A) Guaranteed p95=140 + p99 best-effort with fallback to smaller model (lower price), (B) Dedicated-isolated pool with microbatch=1 -> guaranteed p99=300 (premium).
jamie (Sales): I'll take that to them. Can engineering draft a short one-pager with the numbers + recommended knobs (kernels, microbatch, KV warmup, fallback)? They want something non-technical to show execs.
li (PerfEng): I'll produce a 1-pager: include small profiling table and 3 recommended mitigations (microbatch cap, KV prewarm, prioritized scheduling) + expected cost impact.
alex (EngRuntime): I'll add an appendix with the kernel behavior and a tiny runbook for ops (how to toggle per-customer microbatch and enable KV prewarm).
carla (SRE): I'll write the runbook steps for isolation + monitoring alerts (p99 breach -> auto-scale / rollback to fallback model).
jamie (Sales): Awesome. ETA? FinEdge wants an answer by EOD Friday.
li (PerfEng): I can have the perf slides and numbers by Thursday EOD.
alex (EngRuntime): Engineering notes for the one-pager — include this snippet about scheduler tradeoff:
```
if customer_isolation:
  microbatch_limit = 1
  scheduling_priority = high
else:
  microbatch_limit = default(4)
```
alex (EngRuntime): Also call out that KV hit-rate target >=85% is a gating metric for p95 stability.
priya (Product): Great. Jamies — flag FinEdge that p99 guarantee requires isolation/premium. We'll iterate the exact wording.
jamie (Sales): Will do. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled perf-run v1783 finished (results uploaded to /perf-runs/1783)
